answer.summary: People assumed Apple would build a better YouTube app than YouTube itself, so YouTube had little standing to object. Mehrotra later called that way of thinking silly.

sections.heading: Mistaken assumption
sections.content: Mehrotra said people thought Apple would do a better job building YouTube’s iPhone app, and asked, in effect, “Who are we to tell them not to?” He later called that assumption silly.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately captures both mistaken assumptions in the cited transcript: that Apple would build the app better and that YouTube had no standing to tell Apple not to build it. It directly answers the question and appropriately makes no claim of missing information.

previous_judgments.explanation: The answer accurately reports both mistaken assumptions in the cited transcript: that Apple would build the app better than YouTube, and that YouTube had no standing to tell Apple not to. Mehrotra described that thinking as silly.
